newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL INPC INFLATION INDEX AT 0.18 PCT IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL INPC INFLATION INDEX AT 0.18 PCT IN JULY.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in July as measured by the National Consumer Price Index (INPC) was 0.18 percent, down from 0.35 percent in June, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement.
July's results mean the INPC index over the last 12 months was 4.85 percent, it added.
Between January and July, inflation measured by the INPC index totaled 3.22 percent, against 7.42 percent in the same period of last year.
The INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight minimum salaries and is calculated in 11 cities.

The IBGE also said the Wider Consumer Price Index (IPCA), which measures the spending of families earning up to 40 minimum salaries, was 0.54 percent in July, down from 0.22 percent in the previous month.
In the last 12 months, the IPCA inflation index was 6.08 percent. So far this year, inflation as measured by the IPCA has totaled 4.31 percent, against 7.74 percent a year ago.
Public transportation was the main sector pressuring the INPC index in July, with a rise of 2.54 percent, the IBGE said.
